title: Initiative Thermostat: SLI warranty playbook and automated error-budget reallocation
creator: Riley Chen
description: Summary: Build an "Initiative Thermostat" that enforces an "SLI warranty" — a short-term, measurable guarantee that an initiative may consume a bounded tranche of error budget without triggering organization-level rollout throttles. The thermostat automates tranche allocation, applies sliding gates based on SLI drift signals, and records audit-safe reallocations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console and API: initiatives can request and receive an error-budget tranche; 2) Automated policy engine adjusts tranches when SLI drift crosses thresholds and emits events to the rollout controller; 3) Telemetry dashboard shows allocation history, tranche utilization, and rollback events; 4) End-to-end tests exercising allocation, exceed-and-recover, and forced-revoke scenarios; 5) Audit logs and RBAC for manual overrides.
technical_notes: Key signals: 1-minute SLI rolling burn, 1h burn-rate, and 24h recovery slope. Policy primitives: min/max tranche, cool-down windows, emergency revoke. Implementation plan: policy engine in platform service (policy store + evaluator), webhook to rollout controller, console UI for tranche requests, lightweight DB table for tranche ledger (write-once entries for audit). Data freshness trade-off: faster decisions require lower-latency SLI streams (push vs. batch). Consideration: initial MVP will operate in 'recommendation' mode for one cycle before auto-enforcement to validate thresholds.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives in SLI drift causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require two-tier confirmation (short-term spike detection + sustained anomaly window) and a canary period where adjustments are recommendations only. Risk: wrong tranche sizing may starve initiatives. Mitigation: conservative default tranche sizes and manual override with audit trail.
